subject: Performance gating, MAP and close timeline — OrionHealth (evaluation plan + bench results)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@orionhealth.com>, Victor Huang <vhuang@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Performance gating, MAP and close timeline — OrionHealth (evaluation plan + bench results)

Alyssa / Victor —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our mutual action plan (attached) I wanted to put the performance gating proposal in writing so we have a shared acceptance criteria before the procurement and final signature. Key points:

- Acceptance metrics (must meet at time of final cutover):
  - P95 latency (text generation, 1k tokens prompt, 512 max gen): <= 230ms
  - Throughput: sustained 120 req/s for a single dedicated pool (batching enabled)
  - Time-to-first-token (TTFT): <= 45ms for warmed sessions
  - Concurrency target: 400 concurrent sessions across 2 pools with automatic routing
  - Quality delta: model variant must be within 1.5% of your current baseline in our semantic eval (F1-style set you provided)

- Evaluation plan (short):
  1) Redwood will provide an eval harness and synthetic workload that mirrors your traffic shape (spiky 10s windows every 2 minutes).
  2) We will run three model variants from our catalog (see sheet): base-xxl (float32), base-xxl-quant (4-bit int8-like), and base-large (smaller arch) to show perf/quality tradeoffs.
  3) We will capture per-token latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), TTFT, throughput at target batch sizes, and KV cache hit impact.

- Timeline:
  - 7/21: Redwood executes initial warm runs and shares raw metrics
  - 7/23: Formal MAP checkpoint; bench results + recommendation
  - 7/27: Customer signoff on variant + procurement kickoff

I attached a draft MAP (ORH_MAP_v3.xlsx) and the evaluation spec. Please confirm the gating thresholds above and whether we should add SOC/retention constraints into the MAP now or in procurement.

Thanks,
Marcus
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@orionhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Victor Huang <vhuang@orionhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance gating, MAP and close timeline — OrionHealth (evaluation plan + bench results)

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear write-up. The gating thresholds look reasonable; a couple of asks from our side:

- Can you clarify TTFT measurement method? We need TTFT measured from TCP accept -> first token (not from request serialization).
- Concurrency: 400 sounds fine but we want a midline test at 200 and stress at 800 to see degradation curve.
- Quality delta: we’ll share a 500-example eval pack by EOD 7/20. Please run both exact-match and semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) checks.

If you can incorporate those three changes, we can agree to the MAP and proceed to the bench runs. Procurement wants a placeholder SOW by 7/27; that’s non-negotiable.

—Alyssa
Director, Platform Integrations
OrionHealth

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-21T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance gating, MAP and close timeline — OrionHealth (evaluation plan + bench results)

Alyssa —

Thanks — we’ll adjust the TTFT definition to TCP accept -> first token and add the 200/800 concurrency points. Quick operational notes on the bench:

- Harness: we’ll use the Redwood load generator with the exact request histograms you provided. We’ll seed KV caches to represent warmed sessions and run cold-start passes for the first 10 minutes of each variant.
- Model variants (explicit):
  - redwood/base-xxl-fp32 (baseline perf, best quality)
  - redwood/base-xxl-q4 (4-bit quantized, performance optimized)
  - redwood/base-large-fp16 (smaller, lower cost)

- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT (TCP accept->token), sustained throughput, dropped requests, memory/GPU utilization, and model output similarity (exact + embedding cosine).
- Deliverables: bench CSV, per-variant summary, regression alert if quality delta > 2.0% vs your baseline.

We’ll run initial benching today and share a quick dashboard link. Attaching the updated MAP and the run plan.

Marcus

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@orionhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@orionhealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-23T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance gating, MAP and close timeline — OrionHealth (evaluation plan + bench results)

Alyssa / team —

Quick pricing / SLA note to factor into your SOW draft: if you require the 800-concurrency stress window to be covered by dedicated capacity with an SLA, the committed pool size moves to a larger reserved profile and pricing steps up ~22% vs the standard committed pool we quoted. We can document an interim burst policy (1 hour/day) to limit cost if that helps.

Also confirming we will include cloud-region pinning (us-west) and KMS integration in the SOW draft. Marcus — can you add a language snippet on fallback policy (auto-route to base-large) if 95% capacity hit?

Ben
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-24T14:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance gating, MAP and close timeline — OrionHealth (evaluation plan + bench results)

Alyssa —

Attached are the bench results from our initial runs (orion_bench_results_qc.csv) and the P95 latency chart. Highlights:

- redwood/base-xxl-fp32: p95=220ms, TTFT median=38ms, sustained throughput=130 req/s at target batch sizes, quality delta=+0.2% vs your baseline
- redwood/base-xxl-q4: p95=160ms, TTFT median=30ms, sustained throughput=190 req/s, quality delta=+1.4%
- redwood/base-large-fp16: p95=400ms (under heavy concurrency), TTFT median=60ms, throughput=85 req/s, quality delta=-3.8%

Interpretation/recommendation: base-xxl-q4 (quantized) meets your performance gating and stays within the 1.5% quality threshold. base-large shows cost savings but fails quality. We recommend proceeding with a canary rollout on base-xxl-q4 with automatic fallback to base-xxl-fp32 if semantic similarity drops below threshold during live traffic.

Files attached: ORH_MAP_v3.xlsx, orion_bench_results_qc.csv, latency_p95_concurrency.png

Marissa
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@orionhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, procurement@orionhealth.com
Date: 2026-07-27T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance gating, MAP and close timeline — OrionHealth (evaluation plan + bench results)

Thanks — the numbers look good and the recommendation makes sense. We sign off on the MAP and will proceed with the canary on base-xxl-q4 with fallback policy. Procurement will start SOW edits (we expect a draft by 7/29). Two operational asks before we close:

1) Include explicit monitoring hooks for semantic-similarity drift (embedding cosine) and an automated rollback policy after 10 minutes of continuous degradation.
2) Provide the canary runbook (runbook link in MAP) and on-call contact list.

Once those are in the SOW, we can move to final signature. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alyssa
Director, Platform Integrations
OrionHealth
